note: Shared sound-driver code module (depacked player.pin, loaded into segment 38b7/33a9 by every hardware backend -- Adlib/Roland/SoundBlaster/Beeper/Tandy). Imported as raw x86:LE:16:Real Mode binary with base 0000:0000. GAMEU.EXE's Snd_TriggerEffect/Snd_TriggerEffectRaw far-call into it with AH=command, AL=sound_id. See docs/formats/pin.md. Only 4 of 94 functions named so far -- the rest are unexplored (voice/channel management, SoundBlaster digital-sample service, hardware-detection code). The non-MIDI resource-table-entry mystery (docs/formats/pin.md) was NOT resolved by static analysis -- tracing it through the real per-tick interpreter (Snd_DispatchEventByRunningStatus) produces a reading (note-on) that contradicts the original register-reset guess. Needs dynamic tracing (DOSBox) to settle.

functions.name: Snd_SelectCueForPlayback
functions.summary: Was FUN_0000_231f. Bounds-checks AL (sound ID) against the resource table's own count byte, then selects that cue for playback. Reveals each 4-byte table entry as [2-byte file offset][1 flag byte -> 0xb88, a playback-type flag checked by the AH=1 command dispatcher][1 tempo-scale byte -> 0x2976, folded into FUN_0000_268d's tick-interval computation] -- not one 32-bit offset as a byte-level-only read would suggest, though both extra bytes are 0 in every entry of every shipped .pin file, so a plain 4-byte LE offset read happens to give the right answer anyway. See docs/formats/pin.md's 'Resource-offset table' section.

functions.name: Opl2_WriteRegister
functions.summary: Was FUN_0000_22e3. The genuine OPL2 register-write primitive: DX loaded from a runtime base-port variable [0x1466] (not hardcoded 0x388, since this module is shared across hardware backends); calling convention AH=register, AL=value; write sequence (select-byte out, 6x status-port-read delay, data-byte out to base+1, 35x status-port-read delay) is an exact match for the documented real-hardware OPL2 write-timing requirement (~3.3us/~23us), strong confirmation this is the right function. Called from ~20 voice/channel-management sites (note-on/off, instrument load) reached from normal MIDI-cue playback.

functions.name: Snd_ServiceTick
functions.summary: Was FUN_0000_0206. The real periodic service-tick routine, called every timer interrupt (from the AH=2 command install path, 0x0048/0x009e). Gated on [0xfa] (a hardware-active bitmask): bit1 -> Snd_DispatchEventByRunningStatus; bit0/bit2 -> FUN_0000_0cb0 (an 8-channel loop into FUN_0000_0ce2 plus a countdown-triggered FUN_0000_0cfc call, shaped like SoundBlaster digital-sample/DMA-voice service, unrelated to OPL2). ALSO CONFIRMED this pass: GAMEU.EXE's Game_WarpToLevelStageAndRunLoop (1000:03ff) directly triggers adlib.pin sound ID 11 (one of the non-MIDI resource-table entries, docs/formats/pin.md) via the normal Snd_TriggerEffect(AH=1,AL=11) path -- that content is genuinely live, not dead resource-file padding.

functions.name: Snd_DispatchEventByRunningStatus
functions.summary: Was FUN_0000_2384. Called from Snd_ServiceTick when [0xfa] bit1 is set; gated on [0x2992] (set by Snd_SelectCueForPlayback for every selected cue). Indirect-calls through an 8-entry table DAT_0000_23d4 (read via read_memory) keyed by running-status nibble [0x2991] -- 7 of 8 entries share a handler at 0x23a0 that falls through to the real per-byte reader at 0x23ec (LODSB from [0x297e]; bytes <0x20 -> 16-entry control-code table at 0x23c2; bytes >=0x20 -> note-on handler at 0x256b, note=byte-0x20, frequency-table lookup at 0x29b8, calls FUN_0000_268d). IMPORTANT: tracing adlib.pin's non-MIDI entry 11 (0x63 00 00 01 00 02...) through this exact path reads its first byte (0x63) as a note-on event (note 0x43), NOT a pair-count -- this COMPLICATES the 'OPL2 register-reset sequence' hypothesis (docs/formats/pin.md) rather than confirming it. Static disassembly couldn't settle whether a special-cased raw-register path exists elsewhere or the count-byte reading was simply wrong; recommend dynamic tracing (DOSBox debugger) to resolve.
